title: Two Time Zones
old_caption: Spending the holidays far apart is hard when your clocks don't even agree. Choose one small thing to share at the same moment, like the same dessert, and it starts to feel like a date.

title: Plans Cancelled
old_caption: Dressed up and then the plans fall through? It's okay to feel let down. Let yourself feel it, then make a small cozy plan for the night and a kind rain check for another day.

title: Cried at a Mitten
old_caption: This time of year can bring up a lot, and tiny things might set off big feelings. That's normal. Drink some water, take a short walk, and reach out to someone who understands you.

title: Matching Sweaters
old_caption: Your partner loves an idea that you're not quite comfortable with? Be honest about what feels right for you, then find the version you'll both enjoy. Compromise can be cozy.

title: The long drive home
old_caption: Six hours in one car can test anyone. Snacks for both moods, taking turns on the sound, and one good question in traffic turn a long drive into time together. Save this for the trip home.

title: Two families, one day
old_caption: Two invitations for the same day can feel like a tug of war. Make the plan as a team first, leave room to breathe between visits, and take turns year to year.

title: The gift that missed
old_caption: Opening a gift you don't love can freeze your smile. Thank the thought first, find the part you do like, and if honesty is needed, save it for later and keep it kind.

title: The quiet one
old_caption: Some friends go quiet in December because the month is heavy for them. A no-pressure text and one specific plan can mean more than you know. Who could you check on today?

title: Their family's tradition
old_caption: Walking into someone else's family traditions can feel strange at first. Stay curious, ask how it started, and join in at a level that feels like you. There's usually a sweet story inside.

title: Working the holiday
old_caption: When one of you works the holiday, the day itself can feel lonely. Pick your own date, keep one small ritual, and save a plate instead of a guilt trip.
